about: The moth's hardware and lines (docs/moth-7): what the sailor steers and trims with, and the linkage that makes the wand work the flap. Game frame for x and z (forward from the hull's middle, up from the design waterline), y to port as Blender's, metres. Invented fittings in generic shapes: no maker's parts or names.

tiller.note: a short carbon tiller from the rudder's head forward over the transom; the extension's universal joint at its end

extension.note: the tiller extension, drawn straight forward along the centreline and rising; the twist grip at its end turns a cable down the rudder that sets the elevator's angle (fore-and-aft trim) on top of the steering (MOTH_TwistGrip, socket TwistGrip)

mainsheet.note: the mainsheet: from a block under the boom about 60% of the way out, down to a block on the aft deck, then forward along the deck to a ratchet block by the wings' front bar, where the sailor holds the tail. Drawn two-part between the boom and the deck

vang.note: the vang (kicker): a cascade of rope and two small blocks from the mast's foot to the boom, led aft to the sailor

cunningham.note: a short line from the sail's tack cringle down to a block at the mast's foot, led aft to the sailor beside the vang

pushrod.note: the wand's pushrod: from the wand's pivot along the deck to the main strut's head, where a bellcrank turns it into the rod down the strut to the flap (inside the strut, not drawn); the ride-height adjuster is a knob on the bow fitting, the gearing adjuster a slotted arm at the strut's head

ram.note: the mast's step: a short collar on the deck
